title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages. X is a differentiable manifold, apparently a surface since a circle S_x of half-tangent directions appears. x is a point of X. D_x^* is the 'punctured germ' at x: the germ of X\{x} at x, treated as a pro-space or germ of spaces. A_x is identified with the set of closed cones C in T_x(X) other than {0} and the whole tangent space; equivalently, closed subsets of the direction sphere S_x. Grothendieck wants a canonical equivalence between two groupoids: (i) the fundamental groupoid of D_x^* with 'base points' that are germs of subspaces attached to direction cones; (ii) the fundamental groupoid of S_x. The end goal (next page) is the bijection (80): Isom(gamma, gamma') = Isom_{pi_1(S_x)}(Delta, Delta'). Here gamma, gamma' are differentiable branches issuing from x and Delta, Delta' are their half-tangents. So homotopy classes of paths between two branch base points depend only on the half-tangents.

This page.
1. Choose a local diffeomorphism f: (T_x X, 0) -> (X, x) whose differential at 0 is the identity.
2. For a cone C in A_x, take the cones C' that are strict cone neighbourhoods of C\{0}.
3. Push forward under f the filter base formed by the sets V ∩ (C' - {0}), with V running over neighbourhoods of 0.
4. The resulting filter on X\{x}: (a) does not depend on f, because two such f differ by a map tangent to the identity, which moves a thin cone-sector into any slightly larger cone-sector near 0; (b) tends to x.
5. It therefore defines a germ of space C~ (or A~) over D_x^*.
6. Taking V convex closed, each V ∩ (C' - {0}) is contractible, so the germ C~ is contractible.
7. Functoriality: inclusions C1 ⊂ C2 give inclusions C~1 -> C~2 of germs over D_x^*.
8. This yields the functor (88) from A_x to germs over D_x^*, hence (87) and (81). Using the explicit check (86 bis), this is an equivalence of groupoids.

In modern terms, these sector germs are 'sectorial / tangential base points'. The punctured neighbourhood is shape-equivalent to its link S_x, the boundary circle of the real oriented blow-up. A contractible sector over an arc of directions serves as a base point whose paths are governed by pi_1 of the circle of directions.
errors: The contractibility claim needs a hypothesis. V ∩ (C' - {0}) deformation-retracts (e.g. for V a round ball) onto the direction set of C'. That set is contractible only if C' meets S_x in a contractible set, e.g. an arc in dimension 2.

A general closed cone C ≠ {0}, ≠ T_x(X) (e.g. a union of two rays) has disconnected cone neighbourhoods, so C~ is not contractible. One must restrict A_x to cones whose trace on S_x is an arc or, more generally, contractible, and use cofinal neighbourhoods C' of the same type. Presumably intended, but not stated.
Convexity of V alone does not make V ∩ (C' - {0}) contractible. One needs V star-shaped/radial with respect to rays, such as a ball, or must work with the cone structure.

The independence from f is asserted, not proved. It is true: f'∘f^{-1} = id + o(|v|) maps V ∩ C'' into V' ∩ C' for C'' ⊂ C' strictly and V small. But this is exactly why the filter must be defined via all strict neighbourhoods C', not C itself.

ideas.what: Germ of sector over the punctured neighbourhood D_x^* attached to a cone of tangent directions, defined independently of the chart via the filter of all strictly larger cones
ideas.modern_name: sectorial base point / germ of sector (as in Stokes/asymptotic analysis), real oriented blow-up neighbourhood of an arc of the exceptional circle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malgrange, Sibuya, Deligne (Stokes sectors); A'Campo / Kato–Nakayama (real oriented blow-up, log spaces)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in La Longue Marche (1981) and the Esquisse d'un programme discussion of base points at 'bouts'; not in this explicit form as far as known

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of D_x^* with branch / tangential base points is equivalent to the fundamental groupoid of the circle of half-tangents; paths between branches depend only on their half-tangents
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); Ihara; Nakamura
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (circulated 1981) treats base points at infinity; unsure about this exact formulation

ideas.what: Punctured germ treated as a germ / pro-space with contractible 'points' given by filters tending to x
ideas.modern_name: shape / pro-homotopy type of the link, punctured neighbourhood ≃ link

missed.claim: A chart-independent, purely topological-differentiable construction of tangential base points on a differentiable surface. Arcs of half-tangent directions define contractible sector germs (via filters V ∩ (C' - {0}) over strict cone neighbourhoods), giving a canonical equivalence between the fundamental groupoid of D_x^* with these base points and pi_1 of the circle S_x. This predates or parallels Deligne's 1989 algebraic treatment, which instead uses the tangent vector and the formal or analytic disc.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Shows that Grothendieck developed tangential (indeed sectorial, arc-valued) base points in a differentiable, non-algebraic setting with an explicit groupoid-equivalence argument. This is of historical interest for the attribution of tangential base points and connects to sectorial / Stokes base points.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary once stated, and tangential base points are well established (Deligne). Still, an explicit Grothendieck construction of sector-germ base points with a chart-independence argument, aimed at the bijection Isom(gamma, gamma') = Isom_{pi_1(S_x)}(Delta, Delta'), is a modest unpublished detail of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: The heading is mostly struck out; the surviving sense is 'l'image dans (90) des filtres définis par les ... [du] filtre sur Tang_x(X) formé des V∩(C'-{0})'.

'est évidemment contractile [?]' should probably read: 'Ce germe d'espaces, isomorphe donc au germe d'espaces dans Tang_x(X) muni du filtre défini par la base des V∩(C'-{0}) ... est évidemment contractile.'
The marginal insertion near 'C_1 ⊂ C_2' reads 'C̃_1 → C̃_2' (with a check-mark), indicating the induced morphism of germs.
'd'où (87) et (81)': the '(81)' is a later insertion above the line.
